input.strategy_title: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

An accessibility audit found that four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable,
and focus indicators are inconsistent. Two public-sector customers require an
updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes
and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require
- Flows outside the four audited ones

## Open Questions

None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

# Keyboard accessibility remediation for the four audited core Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic delivers full keyboard operability and consistent visible focus indicators across the four core Dashboard flows named in the accessibility audit: project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission. It resolves every keyboard-related defect enumerated in the audit report — focus lost in modals, controls unreachable via keyboard, and inconsistent focus indicators — so that each flow can be completed end-to-end with keyboard alone.

## Scope

- Remediate all keyboard-accessibility defects the audit report enumerates for the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission), including:
  - Modal focus management: focus moves into the modal on open, is trapped within it while open, and returns to the invoking control on close.
  - Keyboard reachability of every control in the audited flows (no mouse-only interactions).
- Make visible focus indicators consistent across all interactive controls in the audited flows.
- Verify each flow with a manual keyboard-only walk-through (Tab / Shift+Tab / Enter / Space / Arrow keys / Escape as applicable) covering the full happy path of the flow.
- Flows and defects outside the four audited ones, and screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require, are out of scope per the strategy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) can be completed end-to-end using keyboard alone, verified by a manual keyboard-only walk-through of each flow's happy path.
- No focus traps exist outside open modals, and no control in the audited flows is unreachable by keyboard.
- Focus enters each modal on open, remains within it while open, and returns to the invoking control on close, for every modal in the audited flows.
- Visible focus indicators are present and stylistically consistent on every interactive control in the audited flows.
- Every defect enumerated in the audit report for these flows is resolved or explicitly dispositioned with rationale.
- Existing Dashboard automated tests continue to pass with the changes in place.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1):** The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls — this is the core deliverable of this epic.
- **HLR-2 (P1):** Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows — delivered by the same remediation pass over the same four flows and controls.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement)

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation to reflect the fixed state of the four core Dashboard flows: the VPAT (Voluntary Product Accessibility Template) and the product documentation's accessibility statement. Two public-sector customers require an updated, published conformance statement before renewal, so the published documentation is a first-class deliverable of the strategy alongside the code fixes. The documentation work starts after the Dashboard keyboard-accessibility remediation is complete, because it must describe the fixed state.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Update the VPAT to reflect the corrected keyboard operability and focus-indicator conformance of the four audited core flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission).
- Update the product documentation accessibility statement to describe the current conformance state.
- Republish both artifacts through the standard Red Hat documentation content process so the updated conformance statement is publicly available.

Out of scope: screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require, and flows outside the four audited ones (mirroring the strategy's out-of-scope boundaries).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The VPAT accurately reflects the fixed keyboard operability and focus-indicator state of the four audited flows, with no claims that contradict the implemented behavior.
- The product documentation accessibility statement is updated to describe the current conformance state.
- Both documents are republished and publicly accessible at their canonical documentation locations.
- The updated content is technically reviewed against the implemented Dashboard changes by the engineering team that performed the keyboard-accessibility remediation, and review findings are addressed.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P2):** The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review — this epic is the sole deliverable of that requirement.

# Decomposition Summary: RHAISTRAT-9017

## Triage Assessment

This strategy was **not** triaged as below-threshold or docs-only:

- It is not a single-component strategy: the affected components are Dashboard (code changes) and Documentation (content authoring).
- The scope spans two architecturally distinct work streams that warrant separate PR review cycles: front-end code implementation (keyboard operability and focus-indicator fixes in the Dashboard) and substantive content authoring (the updated VPAT and product-docs accessibility statement, HLR-3). The documentation is a first-class deliverable demanded by two public-sector customers, not an incidental touch-up falling out of the code change.
- It is not documentation-only: the Dashboard component requires code changes (HLR-1, HLR-2).

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Keyboard accessibility remediation for the four audited core Dashboard flows | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement) | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Documentation | P2 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 --> RHAISTRAT-9017-E002
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 → RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring blocked by all Implementations) | The conformance documentation must describe the fixed state, so the docs-authoring epic runs after the Dashboard remediation is complete. Per the Step 4 docs-authoring priority exception, this edge does not push E002's P2 priority onto E001 — E001's priority comes from HLR-1/HLR-2 (P1). |

No other edges: there is exactly one code epic and one docs epic; no Investigation epics are needed (the strategy's open questions table is empty and the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow — no unknown changes which epics exist or what they do).

| HLR | Priority | Requirement | Epic(s) | Notes |
|-----|----------|-------------|---------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | Four audited core flows fully operable by keyboard, no focus traps or unreachable controls | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Core scope of the Dashboard remediation epic; audit report enumerates the defects. |

Same priority (P1), so no bundling tension. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | Conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement) updated and republished with technical review | RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Separate work stream: substantive content authoring with a distinct review cycle (Red Hat docs content process), per Step 5 Rule 1 work-product-type boundary. Priority P2 per the docs-authoring exception (strategy frontmatter priority: Normal → P2). |

All three HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Health Warnings

Human verification of these derivations is recommended.
- **Team assumption for Documentation:** the strategy names no owning team for the Documentation component. "RHOAI Documentation" is used as a placeholder assumption; correct it at planning time if the docs work is owned elsewhere.
- **Planning note (epic size):** the Dashboard remediation epic covers four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission). The audit report is stated to enumerate the exact defects per flow, so this is one logical change — a single mechanical accessibility pass over the same surfaces, where a split would fragment the fix pattern and duplicate the audit walk-through. If the defect list turns out to exceed roughly a sprint of effort, re-split by flow. **Re-split trigger:** re-split this epic by audited flow if the audit report's enumerated defects exceed the ~2-week guideline when triaged.
